title: Urban Power Grid Topology and Hierarchy Identification from Open Data
abstract: arXiv:2606.21352v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Understanding the complex topology and hierarchy of urban power grid is crucial for energy prognosis, power flow management, and system resilience analysis. However, detailed grid information remains largely proprietary. This information, nevertheless, is crucial especially for analyzing the last-mile distribution networks connecting individual buildings. This paper addresses this challenge by developing an open-data-driven framework to identify urban power grid topology, from high-voltage transmission down to individual building connections. We integrate public infrastructure data (power-lines, substations, transformers, poles) to map the high and medium-voltage grid skeleton. We then leverage geospatial machine learning on OpenStreetMap building data to cluster loads of building energy demand. translated_title: 基于开放数据的城市电网拓扑与层级识别
translated_abstract: 理解城市电网复杂的拓扑结构和层级关系对于能源预测、潮流管理和系统韧性分析至关重要。然而，详细的电网信息在很大程度上仍属于专有数据。尽管如此，这些信息对于分析连接单个建筑物的“最后一公里”配电网络尤为重要。本文通过开发一个基于开放数据的框架来应对这一挑战，以识别从高压输电到单个建筑连接的城市电网拓扑。我们整合公共基础设施数据（电力线、变电站、变压器、电线杆）来绘制高中压电网骨架。随后，我们利用地理空间机器学习技术对OpenStreetMap建筑数据进行处理，对建筑能耗需求的负荷进行聚类。在聚类的基础上，我们构建了连接聚类建筑与低压配电线路的物理拓扑。
tldr: 本文提出一个基于开放数据的框架，通过整合公共基础设施数据与地理空间机器学习聚类建筑负荷，实现了从高压输电到单个建筑连接的城市电网完整拓扑与层级识别。
